extracted.intended_audience: educated general readers interested in European politics, travel letters, and contemporary accounts of 1848 revolutions
extracted.subtask_description: Composing first-person travel/letter essays that recount political events, public sentiment, speeches, and national declarations while combining descriptive travelogue with political reflection and moral judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and nobleness of official papers/addresses
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Their protest in favor of their rights, their addresses to the Germans at large and the countries under the dominion of Austria, are full of nobleness and thoughts sufficiently great for the use of the coming age.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official political documents and addresses should be noble in tone, elevated in thought, and suited to long-term historical utility; Milanese papers are cited as an example superior in tone compared with more moderate or evasive official papers elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to brotherhood in proclamations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Provisional Government of Milan addresses other nations as 'brothers'—hailing Germans as 'valiant, learned, generous' and urging fraternity, common interests, and moral appeal rather than mere invective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proclamations seeking international sympathy should emphasize shared values and kinship, avoid accusatory blanket condemnations of peoples, and frame appeals in generous, fraternal language (examples: the full translated addresses to the German nation and to peoples under Austria).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify the true adversary (government v. people)
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Our only enemy is the government of Austria...you are not our enemies: you are only instruments in the hand of our foe.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When urging resistance or seeking allies, clearly distinguish the governing regime as the opponent while treating ordinary people of other lands as potential brothers; this framing mitigates ethnic antagonism and broadens appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magnanimity and humanitarian gestures as diplomatic practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The Milanese government offers to 'send back' captured officers and soldiers of various German states and seeks to 'alleviate as much as possible the pains of captivity,' demonstrating magnanimity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include concrete humanitarian measures (e.g., prisoner repatriation) in proclamations to evidence goodwill and to make appeals credible; practical acts reinforce rhetorical brotherhood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusive principles in declarations of faith
rubrics_metrics.description: The Polish declaration of faith includes three articles: 'Every one of the nation a citizen...equal in rights and before authorities'; 'To the Jew...entire equality in political and civil rights'; 'To the companion of life, woman, citizenship, entire equality of rights.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modern political declarations should explicitly guarantee universal citizenship and equal civil/political rights for minorities and women; providing enumerated articles (as in the Polish example) makes commitments clear and progressive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation in victory and humane treatment of defeated
rubrics_metrics.description: The Milanese are praised for 'heroic moderation in victory' and for treating the soldier, once disarmed, as 'only an unfortunate'—rejecting reprisals despite provocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revolutionary movements and governments should avoid revenge and reprisals after conflict; moderation strengthens moral authority and long-term legitimacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral clarity and avoidance of falsehood/evasion in public men
rubrics_metrics.description: Critique of M. Guizot: 'shows his usual shabbiness and falsehood... if there is a cruel, atheistical, treacherous policy, there needs not at least continual evasion to avoid declaring in words what is so glaringly manifest in fact.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public leaders and writers should be candid and avoid evasive rhetoric and falsehood; honesty and moral clarity are ranked higher than rhetorical sophistication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of oratory and presence
rubrics_metrics.description: Mickiewicz's speech produced 'tumult of applause' and 'profound silence'—the author attributes this to 'the force of truth, the great vitality of his presence' and 'magnetism' even when delivered in a foreign language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective public speaking combines truthfulness, moral force, and charismatic presence; rhetorical power can transcend language barriers when sincerity and vitality are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of symbolic public acts and emblems
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: Austrian arms dragged through the streets and burned; the double-headed eagle replaced by an emblem inscribed 'ALTA ITALIA'; throwing pieces into flames as offerings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symbolic acts (burning emblems, replacing symbols) are powerful expressions of popular sentiment and can unify public feeling; such gestures should be meaningful and directed at institutions, not at peoples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Popular philanthropy as measure of civic feeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Accounts of public donation: princes gave large sums; street-pedlers gave daily gains; women gave ornaments down to coral; a ragged man gave 'all I have.' These offerings were accepted and sometimes refused on the ground of compassion (Torlonia refusing a man's dollar to leave it with him).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Widespread voluntary giving—across classes—signals genuine national solidarity and civic virtue; reporting on such acts validates popular commitment and humanizes political movements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel/political letters should mix vivid local description with political reflection
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout the letters the author contrasts physical impressions (Roman winter, larks, Campagna, Carnival rain) with political events and moral reflections on revolutions and constitutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A successful political travel letter blends sensory, local details with informed commentary on events and personalities, using anecdote and scene to illuminate broader political truths and moral judgments.
